nodes.reason: Build the mathematical foundation needed to understand models, optimization, and data transformations.
Vectors, matrices, gradients, and optimization are core to machine learning and deep learning.
Understand gradients, derivatives, and optimization behavior used by model training algorithms.
Statistics supports experiment design, model evaluation, inference, and uncertainty analysis.
Sampling distributions and the CLT are foundational for inference and metric analysis.
Validate assumptions and compare model, product, or business outcomes with statistical rigor.
Probability and sampling methods explain uncertainty, bias, and representativeness in datasets.
Controlled experiments help evaluate product changes, model impact, and business metrics.
Improve experiment power and reduce noise when detecting meaningful changes.
Many production metrics are ratios and need careful variance and interpretation handling.
Econometrics connects statistical modeling with causal and time-dependent real-world data.
Understand regression assumptions, estimators, bias, and causal interpretation before advanced modeling.
Forecasting, regression, and distribution fitting are common data science and analytics tasks.
AI and data roles require practical programming for data pipelines, experiments, and production integration.
Python is the dominant language for data processing, notebooks, machine learning, and AI tooling.
Efficient data structures and algorithms improve data processing and problem-solving capability.
SQL is essential for querying warehouses, preparing datasets, and validating analytical results.
EDA turns raw data into hypotheses, data quality findings, and modeling direction.

nodes.skillName: Data Understanding, Data Analysis and Visualization
nodes.reason: Inspect distributions, missing values, anomalies, relationships, and business meaning before modeling.
Clean, normalize, and validate data so downstream models and dashboards are trustworthy.
Transform raw columns into useful signals for statistical models and machine learning systems.
Use charts and visual summaries to communicate patterns, outliers, and model behavior.
Machine learning provides predictive and pattern-recognition methods for AI/data products.
Learn supervised, unsupervised, ensemble, and neural-network approaches for different data problems.
Classification and regression models solve many labeled prediction problems.
Clustering, dimensionality reduction, and representation methods reveal structure in unlabeled data.
Choose metrics, validation strategies, and baselines to judge model quality reliably.
Deep learning powers modern AI for images, text, speech, recommendation, and generative systems.

nodes.skillName: Fully Connected, CNN, RNN, LSTM, Transformers, Transfer Learning
nodes.reason: Understand the major neural architectures and where each architecture is useful.
Learn layers, activations, losses, backpropagation, regularization, and training loops.
CNNs are a foundation for computer vision and spatial feature extraction.
Sequence models provide historical context for language, time series, and event data.
Transformer architectures are central to modern NLP, multimodal AI, and foundation models.
Reuse pretrained models to reduce data requirements and accelerate practical AI applications.
Production AI work needs repeatable deployment, monitoring, governance, and lifecycle management.
Package, test, deploy, and roll back models through reliable automated workflows.
Expose trained models through batch jobs, APIs, streaming systems, or embedded runtimes.
Track latency, errors, drift, data quality, and model performance after deployment.
AI data engineers need reliable data movement, transformation, and orchestration for model-ready datasets.
Design extraction, transformation, loading, and warehouse-first processing flows.
Schedule, retry, monitor, and dependency-manage data workflows for reproducible AI pipelines.
Validate schema, freshness, completeness, ranges, and anomalies before data reaches models.
